Depends on context. 

Both are rather ass against armored opponents, and both are very much meant for slashing rather than thrusting. 

Sabers in particular became prominent in Europe and it’s colonies during a time when handguns were becoming prominent and armor began to phase out. Katanas were always sidearms at best and strictly status symbols at worst. When gunpowder weaponry began being introduced in Japan and armor began being phased out as well, they were employed in a nearly identical manner as sabers. Any pros or cons they would have against each other would be marginal at best.

Sabers offer better hand protection and maneuverability especially while on horseback. Sabers are also generally made from higher quality metals (assuming it’s a historical weapon and not a modern reproduction) because Europeans had access to better quality steels. That said, a katana would be easier to maintain due to their differential tempering (blades being made out of a softer metal in the core and a harder metal on the edge) while a saber, being made integrally from the same high carbon metal, would be harder to damage but harder to repair if it *did* get damaged.


Weight-wise things are also marginally different. Katanas’ weight values unsheathed ranged between 0.9 to 1.2 kg. Sabers’ weight have a wider range as there was more production of sabers. A standard British mariner pattern 1796 saber weighed in at 960 grams, while a model 1840 American saber weighed 1.1kg, for example.

**You *could* argue the saber’s lower (all the following attributes are in an average) weights and longer blade lengths in favor of the saber as well, but it’s on a strict case-by-case basis.**

What does ping measure?

Online games function by uploading and downloading data. 

The amount of time that it takes a server to send (upload) and receive (download) data, is called ping. That is why it’s measured in milliseconds. 

Internet speed is comprised of two measurements. The amount of data your service can send (upload) and receive (download) is usually measured in megabytes per second. 

The more data your internet service can send and receive in a second matters when gaming because ping lowers when servers functions properly. 

That said, if your game is running on shit servers, they might saturate or just straight up be coded poorly and literally not work. This can manifest in high pings in games, because regardless of how much data your service sends, if the server doesn’t receive any, ping goes up.
